subject: Clarify: ISO scope alignment + evidence escrow decision criteria for certification readiness
messages:
From: Zoe Park <zoe.park@acmefs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-security@acmefs.com
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scope & escrow question ahead of intake

Kimberly —

Thanks for taking this on. Two quick asks from the Acme side as we finalize the intake for ISO/FedRAMP scoping:

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood intends to treat the FedRAMP authorization boundary as a superset of the ISO scope for the upcoming assessments, or do you want the ISO evidence set to be limited to the ISO service boundary only? Our procurement and InfoSec folks need the decision so we can map our controls and prepare an evidence bundle.

2) For evidence escrow and sample windows: what is Redwood's default retention snapshot cadence (daily/hourly) and how long are snapshots kept for auditor sampling? Alicia from AuditCo is cc'd — any expectations from the auditor side would help.

We're attaching a rough boundary draft and a proposed evidence index for your review. Ideally we'd have a short call next week to lock decisions and owners.

Best,
Zoe
Head of Contracts — Acme Financial Services

Attachments: boundary-draft_v2.pdf, evidence-index.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Park <zoe.park@acmefs.com>
Cc: Alicia Rivera <alicia.rivera@auditco.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scope & escrow question ahead of intake

Zoe — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the draft. Short answers up front, with proposed decision criteria below: 

- High-level: We propose that for this program the FedRAMP authorization boundary be treated as the superset for operational controls (network, enclave, KMS), and the ISO scope will be aligned to that same boundary for evidence collection. That reduces dual-mapping work and simplifies auditor sampling.

Decision criteria that led us here:
- Customer-facing data flows must be fully included in the boundary.
- Any infrastructure that stores or processes customer data (KV caches, model artifacts, snapshot exports) is included.
- Where third-party managed services are in scope for FedRAMP but out of ISO (e.g., certain cloud PaaS components), we will include them in the FedRAMP narrative and provide attestation + control narratives to satisfy ISO auditors (exceptions documented).

For evidence escrow and snapshots: our standard is daily snapshots retained for 30 days, with a 90-day archival window for audited customers on request. For FedRAMP scoping we can commit to a 90-day retention for the audit sample window; please confirm if that meets Acme/AuditCo needs.

Propose a 30-minute working session Monday 10/5 at 11am PT to lock owners and timelines. Action owners I propose: Soojin (technical evidence), Marissa (compliance coordination), me for decisions and executive escalations.

I attached a quick markup to your boundary PDF (see boundary-draft_v2.pdf).

Thanks — Kim
Director, Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: boundary-draft_v2.pdf (annotated)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scope & escrow question ahead of intake (technical notes)

Kim / team — quick tech notes to support the decision: 

- Snapshots: current infra supports daily and hourly snapshots for critical enclaves. Daily is the default for app-level state; we can enable hourly for the model-enclave for the audit window (extra cost).
- KMS / key rotation: keys are rotated every 90 days by default; we can include rotation logs and CMK policies in the evidence package.
- Logs & retention: production request traces and auth logs are retained for 60 days in hot storage; we can export to archive for 1 year on request. For FedRAMP samples we should capture a 90-day contiguous window (request traces + access reviews).
- Evidence handoff: recommend a staged handoff: (1) internal evidence index (redacted) -> (2) secure file share with Acme -> (3) notarized escrow dump if requested by auditor.

Questions for AuditCo (Alicia): what level of redaction is acceptable for PII in sample logs versus needing a separate data-masked snapshot?

Sooj
Sr. Infra Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Team — follow-up after our working session and internal review. Summary of decisions, owners, and near-term asks: 

Decisions (agreed):
- ISO scope will align with the FedRAMP authorization boundary for this engagement to avoid dual-scope divergence.
- Snapshot cadence for audit sampling: enable daily snapshots retained 90 days for Acme-specific audit window. For the model enclave, enable hourly snapshots for the 90-day window (Aditya to confirm cost impact).
- Evidence handoff: staged handoff (internal index -> secure share -> escrow dump if requested). Any PII in log samples will be masked; Alicia to confirm masking threshold.

Owners & action items:
- Soojin Lee: prepare technical evidence package and enable hourly snapshots for model enclave (due 2026-10-13).
- Marissa Cole: coordinate intake forms and compile compliance narrative / control crosswalk (due 2026-10-11).
- Aditya Rao: produce estimated cost delta for hourly snapshot retention and confirm storage/egress constraints (due 2026-10-09).
- Kimberly Park: finalize scope decision and produce decision memo for Acme + exec sign-off (due 2026-10-08).

Attachments to be published to Acme secure share once Soojin and Marissa sign off: evidence-index.csv, fedramp-scope-diagram.png.
